title: 1989 AHSME Problem 8
statement: For how many integers \(n\) between \(1\) and \(100\) does \(x^2+x-n\) factor into the product of two linear factors with integer coefficients?

solutions.text:
An integer factorization must have the form \((x-k)(x+k+1)\) for some positive integer \(k.\) Expanding gives \(x^2+x-k(k+1),\) so \(n=k(k+1).\) The values \(k=1,2,\ldots,9\) give \(n\le100,\) while \(10\cdot11\gt100.\) There are \(9\) values.

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the factors as \((x-r)(x+s)\) with positive integers \(r,s\)
The coefficient of \(x\) forces the two integer parameters to differ by \(1\)
